rounds.text: IKOMA Technologies Limited is demonstrating extraordinary and sustained compounding capabilities over multiple time horizons, evidenced by a 10-year compounded profit growth of 23% [E15], a 5-year compounded profit growth of 42% [E16], and a 3-year compounded profit growth of 34% [E17]. This exceptional earnings expansion is further validated by a strong medium-term return on equity track record, boasting a 3-year median ROE of 30% [E21] and a verified 3-year ROE of 29.8% [E51]. Conceded: trailing twelve-month profit growth sits at -83% [E18], sales dropped 100% year-over-year [E62], and the current P/E ratio is elevated at 666x [E1].

IKOMA Technologies Limited is currently trading at an extreme valuation, evidenced by a P/E ratio of 666x [E1] and a P/B ratio of 16.62x [E2], both of which vastly exceed their respective sector benchmarks of 23.64x and 2.58x [E6, E7]. This disconnect between price and performance is further highlighted by the fact that price growth has outpaced profit growth by 97%, signaling that market expectations are running significantly ahead of actual delivery [E48]. The company’s operational efficiency is concerning, with an ROA of 1.23% compared to a sector benchmark of 4.68% [E8] and a recent ROE that has plummeted to 3% [E22, E63]. Furthermore, the trailing twelve months have seen a sharp contraction in profit growth of -83% [E18], and the company reports a sales decline of 100% YoY [E62]. Conceded: the company has demonstrated a strong 10-year compounded profit growth of 23% [E15] and a 3-year median ROE of 30% [E21, E51]. Despite these historical figures, the current lack of dividend yield [E4] combined with the recent collapse in growth metrics suggests that the current market capitalization of ₹ 153 Cr is unsupported by the firm's immediate financial reality [E3, E18, E62].

The bull’s reliance on historical compounding [E15, E16, E17] ignores the reality that current performance has collapsed, evidenced by a trailing twelve-month profit growth of -83% [E18] and a catastrophic 100% year-over-year decline in sales [E62]. While the bull highlights a 3-year median ROE [E21, E51], this metric is rendered obsolete by the most recent data showing ROE has plummeted to 3% [E22, E63], which is significantly lower than the sector benchmark of 10.43% [E9]. Conceded: the company has a historical 3-year ROE track record of 29.8% [E51]. This historical performance cannot justify a P/E ratio of 666x [E1] or a P/B ratio of 16.62x [E2], both of which are vastly higher than their respective sector benchmarks [E6, E7]. Furthermore, the market is currently pricing the stock based on expectations that are not being met, as price growth exceeds profit growth by 97% [E48]. Ultimately, the company’s ROA of 1.23% [E8] is far below the sector benchmark of 4.68%, confirming that the business is failing to generate efficient returns on its assets in the current environment.
